metadataReview.note: Reviewed Gregorian date: 11 July 1690. OPW explicitly calls 1 July Old Style; the Irish public libraries’ visitor-centre account explicitly gives 11 July according to the modern calendar. Cached P585 contains both 11 July Gregorian and 1 July Julian; the selected raw numerical date had lost this distinction. This is the date of the engagement, not the later 12 July commemoration. The prior Kingdom of Scotland (Q230791) item and P710 citations are also preserved as historical participant provenance. Those two citations do not establish a unique coalition assignment or a separate Scottish count and are not used as calendar evidence.

note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 43, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the exact whole battle on 11 July 1690 Gregorian, conditional on the separately proposed calendar correction. OPW explicitly labels 1 July Old Style; the Irish libraries’ visitor-centre account supplies 11 July in the modern calendar. Local force identities describe Williamite and Jacobite aggregate armies, not exclusively English troops or present-day states. OPW gives 36000 Williamite and 25000 Jacobite personnel; CDB90 retains its own 35000 and 23000 estimates and its distinct casualty estimates. The institutional total difference is disclosed rather than averaged or silently reconciled. Both source strengths are initial totals without reinforcements. The former five published participant entries are replaced by two aggregate coalition armies. Their original item/statement citations are retained with the corresponding aggregates, except Kingdom of Scotland (Q230791), whose ambiguous camp-level identity is preserved among battle metadata sources. No five-to-two identity retention is claimed and no unknown national component is added on top of either coalition total. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name ENG ARMY): OPW identifies the aggregate army led by William III. The original ENG ARMY is retained as provenance but is not displayed as an exclusively English force. OPW’s 36000 differs from CDB90’s 35000. Historical published participant Q4111409 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component. Historical published participant Q170072 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name ENG & IRISH REB ARMY): OPW identifies the aggregate army led by James II. The local name clarifies ENG & IRISH REB ARMY without distributing its total among national contingents. OPW’s 25000 differs from CDB90’s 23000. Historical published participant Q212983 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component. Historical published participant Q70972 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component.
